ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $1,772,555, reflecting an increase of $236,514, or 15.4%, as compared to $1,536,041 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the increase in sales commissions related to the increase in sales revenue.

sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $1,772,555, reflecting an increase of $236,514, or 15.4%, as compared to $1,536,041 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to the increase in sales commissions related to the increase in sales revenue.

da_op.text: Depreciation and amortization for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $208,428, reflecting an increase of $22,135, or 11.9%, as compared to $186,293 for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

nonop.text: Total other income for the six months ended September 30, 2026 was income of $108,677, reflecting a decrease of $69,530, as compared to income of $178,207 for the six months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was attributable to a decrease in interest income earned on our cash and increase in interest expense on equipment line of credit.

tax.text: Provision (benefit) for income taxes was ($262,109) and $0 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The benefit for income taxes for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was principally attributable to a federal and state tax provision of $38,149, (net of utilization of net operation loss and tax credit carryforwards utilized during the period) and a true-up of state refunds receivable in the amount of $184,810, offset by a benefit of $485,068 for the release of a portion of the Company’s net deferred tax asset valuation allowance. The provision for income taxes for the three months ended September 30, 2025 was principally attributable to the loss before income taxes for the period and the impact of recording a full valuation allowance on the Company’s deferred tax assets, net.

net.text: As of September 30, 2026, and March 31, 2026, the Company’s cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash was $10,003,700 and $9,647,698, respectively. The Company has recorded net income of $2,017,880 and net loss of $681,479 for the six months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. As of September 30, 2026, and March 31, 2026, the Company had working capital of $21,389,638 and $18,937,744 and stockholders’ equity of $24,927,922 and $22,358,492, respectively.

ocf.text: Our principal source of liquidity has been from cash flows generated by operating activities and our cash reserves.

da.text: Depreciation and amortization for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $208,428, reflecting an increase of $22,135, or 11.9%, as compared to $186,293 for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

wc.text: Our primary requirements for liquidity and capital are working capital, inventory, capital expenditures, and general corporate needs. We expect these needs to continue as we further develop and grow our business. For the six months ended September 30, 2026, our primary source of liquidity came from our operating cash flows. Based on our current plans and business conditions, we believe that existing cash, together with cash generated from operations will be sufficient to satisfy our anticipated cash requirements in fiscal year 2027 and into fiscal year 2028, and we are not aware of any trends or demands, commitments, events or uncertainties that are reasonably likely to result in a decrease in liquidity of our assets. We may require additional capital to respond to technological advancements, competitive dynamics or technologies, business opportunities, challenges, acquisitions or unforeseen circumstances and in either the short-term or long-term may determine to engage in equity or debt financings or enter into additional credit facilities for other reasons. If we are unable to obtain adequate financing or financing on terms satisfactory to us, when we require it, our ability to continue to grow or support our business and to respond to business challenges could be significantly limited.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the year ended March 31, 2026, two customers accounted for 34.0% of the Company’s net revenues, each represented 23.5% and 10.5%, respectively.
During the year ended March 31, 2025, two customers accounted for 31.9% of the Company’s net revenues, each represented 17.8% and 14.1%, respectively.

These sales representatives accounted for approximately 75% of the Company’s net sales for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (with the balance of Company net sales being generated via direct customer contact).
